newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals firmer after overnight gains.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals firmer after overnight gains.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metal futures ended higher in Friday, aligning themselves with gains in the spot market overnight, traders said.

A recovery in the dollar after it briefly slipped below 111 yen early in the day also helped precious metal futures close at or near their intraday highs, although traders said activity in the futures markets was sluggish. Yen-based futures prices tend to rise when the yen weakens against the dollar.
TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold settled five yen higher at 1,354 yen per gram, the intraday high and matching a life-of-contract high set earlier in the week.
Gold bullion closed at $382.00/30 an ounce, virtually unchanged from New York's Thursday closing quote of $382.00/50.

After the $382 resistance mark was breached in New York trade overnight, Japanese traders put the next resistance at $383.50, while one reported good support from professional buying around $381.50 during Friday's Asian trading hours.

The market will be monitoring U.S. producer price data due at 1230 GMT for any possible reaction in the bond and stock markets. Analysts' average forecasts were for a 0.3 percent gain in the overal September producer price index and a 0.2 percent rise in the core rate, which excludes food and energy.
TOCOM most-active August platinum rallied to a one-month high of 1,377 yen per gram, before retracing to close at 1,374 yen, up eight. Bullion ended at $387.50/$388.25 an ounce.

One trade house source said a large speculative long position held by individual investors in the December TOCOM contract continued to weigh on the market, while industrial demand for physical platinum was also sluggish. He said support for the bullion price was solid, however, at $382 an ounce.
TOCOM August palladium ended at 426 yen per gram, up two yen, while August silver was up 4.7 at 182.4 yen per 10 grams.
